Question 58

Which of the following commands is used to save any transaction permanently into the database?

  • A. Rollback
  • B. None of the choices are correct
  • C. Savepoint
  • D. Commit

Source

  • Mock exam 2 · Question 12

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Distinguish completing a transaction from marking an intermediate recovery position.

Study-guide sections

ADB06 · Transactions, ACID and state transitions

ADB-S02 · Transaction boundaries and savepoints

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

ADB06 · Transactions, ACID and state transitions

ADB-S02 · Transaction boundaries and savepoints

Correct answer: D — Commit

COMMIT successfully completes the transaction and requests a durable committed outcome. ROLLBACK instead cancels uncommitted changes. SAVEPOINT marks an intermediate position to which later work can be rolled back, retaining earlier work within the same transaction; it neither completes that transaction nor makes the retained changes independently durable. Because COMMIT is offered, the none-of-the-choices alternative is false. D therefore identifies the permanent transaction-completion command.

Evidence in the complete study note

In SQL transaction-block notation, BEGIN starts a block, COMMIT completes it successfully, and ROLLBACK cancels its uncommitted changes. Committing requests a durable transaction outcome; it is distinct from merely finishing the last read or write operation.ADB-S02
SAVEPOINT marks an intermediate position inside the current transaction. ROLLBACK TO discards changes made after that position while retaining earlier work in the transaction. A savepoint is not an independent durable commit, and rolling back to it does not itself commit the retained changes.ADB-S02

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Incorrect: ROLLBACK cancels uncommitted work rather than accepting it permanently.

B · incorrect — Incorrect: COMMIT is offered and is the requested completion command.

C · incorrect — Incorrect: SAVEPOINT marks an intermediate rollback position inside the still-open transaction; it does not commit.

D · correct — Correct: COMMIT completes the transaction successfully and requests a durable outcome.

Which one of the following is NOT correct about transaction failure?

  • B. Catastrophes can be a cause of transaction failure

ADB26 · Classify failures and choose the starting resource

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

ADB26 · Classify failures and choose the starting resource

Correct answer: C — Concurrency control enforcement avoids transaction failure

The failure list includes logical programming errors, disk blocks losing data, and physical catastrophes. It also explicitly says concurrency enforcement may abort a transaction for serializability or deadlock (p.98). Thus claiming it avoids transaction failure is the incorrect statement.

Evidence in the complete study note

Transaction failures include invalid operations, constraint violations and concurrency-control aborts. Enforcing concurrency can deliberately abort work; it does not prevent every transaction failure. A system crash loses volatile memory while disks may survive. Media failure damages persistent storage and normally requires restoring a backup, then replaying available archived logs. Human mistakes may require point-in-time restoration before the bad committed operation.ADB26

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Logical errors are explicitly a cause.

B · incorrect — Physical problems and catastrophes are explicitly listed.

C · correct — Concurrency enforcement itself may abort transactions, contradicting the absolute claim.

D · incorrect — Loss of disk-block data is explicitly listed.

Question 63

Which listed policy prevents lock-wait deadlock without comparing transaction-age timestamps? Here 'wait-wait' means allowing every conflicting request to wait with no ordering or cycle restriction.

  • A. Wait-wait
  • B. No-wait
  • C. Wound-wait
  • D. Wait-die

Adapted from

  • MOE Computer Science Exit Exam · Question 14-1

  • National Computer Science Exit Exam · Question 100

  • National Computer Science Exit Exam

  • MOE Computer Science Exit Exam

  • Computer Science Exit Exam practice collection · Question 63

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Distinguish a waiting cycle, a long wait and indefinite unfair postponement.

Study-guide sections

ADB13 · Deadlock detection, prevention and starvation

ADB14 · Wait–die and wound–wait: compare requester and holder

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

ADB13 · Deadlock detection, prevention and starvation

ADB14 · Wait–die and wound–wait: compare requester and holder

Correct answer: B — No-wait

No-wait aborts immediately when a lock request conflicts, so transactions cannot form a lock-wait cycle and no age comparison is needed. Wait–die and wound–wait use relative transaction ages to decide who waits or aborts. Under the explicitly defined wait-wait alternative, every conflicting request may wait without a cycle-prevention restriction, so a transaction can hold one item while waiting for another in a cycle. That alternative therefore fails the deadlock-prevention requirement.

Evidence in the complete study note

Fixed resource ordering and conservative 2PL prevent cycles. A no-wait policy aborts immediately on an incompatible lock request and needs no age timestamp. A timeout aborts long waits but may mistake slow progress for deadlock. Starvation is indefinite postponement while other work proceeds, without a required cycle. Fair queues, sensible victim selection and retaining original transaction timestamps on retry reduce starvation; deadlock freedom alone does not prove fairness.ADB13
A smaller timestamp means an older transaction. In wait–die, an older requester may wait for a younger holder; a younger requester needing an older holder aborts itself. In wound–wait, an older requester aborts the younger holder; a younger requester waits for the older holder. Always identify requester versus holder before applying the names.ADB14

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Incorrect: unrestricted waiting permits a hold-and-wait cycle, so this defined policy does not prevent deadlock.

B · correct — Correct: immediate abort on a conflicting request prevents lock waits without comparing ages.

C · incorrect — Incorrect: wound–wait compares requester and holder ages to choose waiting or aborting a younger holder.

D · incorrect — Incorrect: wait–die compares ages to choose whether the requester waits or aborts.

ADB37 · Replication policies and their costs

ADB36 · Fragmentation: correctness and reconstruction

ADB33 · Distributed, homogeneous and heterogeneous systems

ADB42 · NoSQL families, wide columns and CAP

Correct answer: A — A. Replication

Replication creates additional copies of selected data and can improve read locality by placing them near users. That directly satisfies the specified regional read-copy requirement. D · incorrect — Partitioning divides data; by itself it creates no spare copy.

Question 67

In a generic DBMS component model applied to a MySQL deployment, which specialized role coordinates restoring valid data from stored backups and logs after data loss? Use generic functional roles, not claims about named MySQL engine internals.

  • A. Buffer Manager
  • B. Transaction Manager
  • C. Query Engine
  • D. Recovery Manager

Adapted from

  • Computer Science Exit Exam · Sene 2016 · Question 32-1

  • Computer Science Exit Exam practice collection · Question 70

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Identify what failed, what durable resources survive and which restoration action is required.

Study-guide sections

ADB26 · Classify failures and choose the starting resource

ADB07 · Read/write operations, buffers and log records

ADB06 · Transactions, ACID and state transitions

ADB17 · Query processing: representation before execution

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

ADB26 · Classify failures and choose the starting resource

ADB07 · Read/write operations, buffers and log records

ADB06 · Transactions, ACID and state transitions

ADB17 · Query processing: representation before execution

Correct answer: D — D. Recovery Manager

Recovery is the specialized responsibility for restoring valid database state after failure or loss. Backups supply a separate stored copy, and available logs can restore later recoverable changes. The recovery-manager role therefore matches the question's generic component model. Buffer management caches working pages; transaction management is the broader parent responsibility, while the query engine processes requests. This makes no claim about MySQL's internal module names.

Evidence in the complete study note

Transaction failures include invalid operations, constraint violations and concurrency-control aborts. Enforcing concurrency can deliberately abort work; it does not prevent every transaction failure. A system crash loses volatile memory while disks may survive. Media failure damages persistent storage and normally requires restoring a backup, then replaying available archived logs. Human mistakes may require point-in-time restoration before the bad committed operation.ADB26
Generic recovery-manager terminology should not be mistaken for an exact MySQL component specification.ADB26
A full backup copies the database to separate storage; scheduled backups plus archived logs support restoration to a chosen recoverable point.ADB26

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Buffers cache working data and are not durable backup copies.

B · incorrect — Transaction management is broader than the specialized restoration role requested.

C · incorrect — A query engine processes queries rather than coordinating restoration.

D · correct — The generic recovery role coordinates restoration using durable recovery resources.

Question 69

Business people always remodel their business by closely studying their customers' purchasing habits over the course of their purchase history. Accordingly, a salesperson at Markato shop noticed that people who always buy shoes will also buy socks with probability of 0.75 and hence decided to put shoes and socks side by side for ease of accessibility. Which big data analytics technique could this salesperson could employ?

  • A. Association rule
  • B. Clustering algorithm
  • C. Predictive modeling
  • D. Regression modeling

Source

  • Computer Science model exam collection · Question 30

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Classify the actual content or pattern being analyzed rather than the storage product.

Study-guide sections

ADB43 · Data sources and association rules

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

ADB43 · Data sources and association rules

Correct answer: A — Association-rule mining: shoes ⇒ socks has confidence 0.75.

The observation is a conditional co-purchase pattern: among shoe purchases, socks also appear with probability 0.75. ADB43 defines this as the confidence of an association rule and explicitly distinguishes co-occurrence mining from clustering, classification and numeric regression. The store-layout decision uses that rule; it does not change the underlying technique or prove causation.

Evidence in the complete study note

An association rule X⇒Y describes co-occurrence. Support=count(X and Y)/N; confidence=count(X and Y)/count(X)=P(Y|X). If 75 of 100 shoe purchases include socks, confidence(shoes⇒socks)=0.75. This does not prove causation or specify support without total transaction count. Clustering groups similar cases without target labels; classification predicts categories and regression predicts numeric outcomes. Purchasing co-occurrence is association mining even when its result informs store layout.ADB43

Choice by choice

A · correct — The rule captures shoe/sock co-occurrence with conditional confidence 0.75.

B · incorrect — Clustering groups similar cases without target labels rather than directly discovering this co-purchase rule.

C · incorrect — The stated evidence is an association rule, not a separately specified predictive modeling task.

D · incorrect — Regression predicts numeric outcomes rather than identifying this purchasing co-occurrence rule.

Under the stated convention, training first produces the model. Testing then measures it on held-out data, and evaluation uses those results to decide whether business criteria justify deployment. C follows that sequence. Evaluation during model selection can use a different ordering, but this question explicitly assigns evaluation to the subsequent release review, so the other sequences misplace that review.

CRISP-DM starts with business understanding: define the decision and success criteria. Then understand data, prepare it, model, evaluate and deploy; the process is iterative. Cleaning, integration and feature selection occur during preparation, not before the business problem exists.ADB44
If an MCQ asks training→testing→evaluation→deployment, state that convention; another valid workflow can evaluate during model selection before final testing.ADB44

Question 72

What is the defining purpose of a transaction in database management?

  • A. To secure the database from unauthorized access
  • B. To optimize query performance
  • C. To group database operations into one logical unit of work
  • D. To define the structure and organization of a database

Adapted from

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 162

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Track the transaction's guarantee or lifecycle boundary described by the scenario.

Study-guide sections

ADB06 · Transactions, ACID and state transitions

ADB11 · Locks, compatibility, conversion and managers

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

ADB06 · Transactions, ACID and state transitions

ADB11 · Locks, compatibility, conversion and managers

Correct answer: C — C. To group database operations into one logical unit of work

A transaction groups database operations into one logical unit of work. The DBMS supports its atomicity, consistency, isolation and durability requirements, including controlled interference with concurrent transactions. Grouping is the defining concept, rather than query tuning, access authorization or schema construction. Read-only work can also form a transaction, so the definition is not limited to operations that change stored data.

Evidence in the complete study note

A transaction is a logical unit of database work, including read-only work. Atomicity means all effects or none; consistency means correct work preserves integrity rules; isolation controls concurrent interference; durability preserves committed effects despite failure. A DBMS cannot automatically make incorrect business logic consistent.ADB06
A transaction must own the appropriate lock before access and can release only its own locks.ADB11
One transaction may request a lock on an already locked item: it is granted if compatible, otherwise waits or aborts under the policy.ADB11

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Authorization governs who may access data rather than defining transaction grouping.

B · incorrect — Optimization chooses query execution strategies.

C · correct — A transaction is one logical unit of database work.

D · incorrect — Schema definition describes data structures rather than a unit of work.

Question 73

A correctly implemented financial transaction must preserve a declared total-balance invariant when it completes. Which ACID property names preservation of such integrity rules? Focus on the invariant rather than partial execution, concurrent interference or survival after a crash.

  • B. Consistency
  • C. Isolation
  • D. Durability

Study-guide sections

ADB06 · Transactions, ACID and state transitions

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

ADB06 · Transactions, ACID and state transitions

Correct answer: B — B. Consistency

Consistency means that correct transactional work preserves declared integrity rules. Maintaining the total-balance invariant is therefore the consistency requirement. Atomicity addresses whether the effects happen together, isolation controls interference among concurrent transactions and durability preserves committed effects after failure. These properties cooperate, but the revised question identifies invariant preservation as the particular guarantee to name.

Evidence in the complete study note

A transaction is a logical unit of database work, including read-only work. Atomicity means all effects or none; consistency means correct work preserves integrity rules; isolation controls concurrent interference; durability preserves committed effects despite failure. A DBMS cannot automatically make incorrect business logic consistent.ADB06

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Atomicity names all-or-none effects rather than invariant preservation itself.

B · correct — Consistency names preservation of declared integrity rules by correct work.

D · incorrect — Durability preserves committed effects after failure.

Question 74

In the object-oriented model, an object is defined as:

  • A. An instance of a class
  • B. A collection of attributes
  • C. A primary key in a database
  • D. A relationship between tables

Source

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 185

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Distinguish an object instance from its class, attribute values and persistent identity.

Study-guide sections

ADB01 · Objects, identity, classes and persistence

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

ADB01 · Objects, identity, classes and persistence

Correct answer: A — An instance of a class.

ADB01 explicitly distinguishes a class specification from each object instantiated from it. A class defines available attributes and operations, while an object is one individual instance with identity, state and behavior. A collection of attributes omits identity and behavior; a key or an intertable relationship belongs to a different relational description.

Evidence in the complete study note

An object combines identity, state and behavior. A class specifies the attributes and operations of its instances; an object is one instance. The object identifier (OID) distinguishes objects independently of their attribute values and remains stable over that object's lifetime. Two objects can have equal values and different identities; changing a name does not create a new identity.ADB01
Complex CAD or multimedia structures can suit an object model, but many-to-many relationships alone do not require abandoning relational design.ADB01
An object-relational DBMS extends a relational system with richer types; ORM maps programming objects into relational tables.ADB01

Choice by choice

A · correct — An object is an individual instance of a class with its own identity and state.

B · incorrect — Attributes describe state but omit the identity and behavior that also characterize an object.

C · incorrect — A database primary key is an identifier constraint, not the definition of an object instance.

D · incorrect — A relationship between tables is a relational association rather than an object instance.

Question 75

Study-guide sections

ADB02 · Encapsulation, abstraction and object associations

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

ADB02 · Encapsulation, abstraction and object associations

Correct answer: B — Hiding and controlling access to internal object details.

ADB02 describes encapsulation as grouping state with operations and controlling access to implementation details. A withdrawal method can enforce rules while hiding storage. B states the relevant information-hiding aspect. Combining classes, associating objects and defining subtype hierarchies are distinct activities; none describes the encapsulation boundary around an object's state and operations.

Evidence in the complete study note

Encapsulation groups state with operations and controls access to implementation details. Account.withdraw(amount) can enforce a balance rule while hiding its storage. Abstraction presents the relevant contract—what withdrawal does—without exposing how it is implemented. These ideas overlap in information hiding, but combining state and methods specifically describes encapsulation.ADB02
A class defines structure and behavior; an attribute describes state; a method implements an operation.ADB02
It is different from inheritance, which means an is-a relationship between types.ADB02

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Encapsulation groups an object's state and operations, not multiple classes into one entity.

B · correct — Encapsulation controls access to the internal representation behind the object's operations.

C · incorrect — Links between objects are associations rather than encapsulation itself.

D · incorrect — Superclass/subclass structure concerns inheritance rather than information-hiding boundaries.

ADB03 · Inheritance, polymorphism and safe substitutability

Study-guide references

ADB03 · Inheritance, polymorphism and safe substitutability

Correct answer: B — Inherit applicable attributes and behavior from a superclass.

ADB03 defines inheritance as deriving a subtype from a superclass and reusing its applicable attributes and behavior. B captures that idea. It does not inherently require multiple parents, dynamically create objects, or merely link unrelated objects. Those alternatives concern particular inheritance forms, instantiation or association rather than the general meaning of inheritance.

Evidence in the complete study note

Inheritance derives a subtype from a superclass, reusing applicable attributes and behavior. GraduateStudent is a Student; association instead says Student belongs to Department. EER teaches inherited attributes and relationships, while a programming object model also specifies behavior.ADB03

A · incorrect — Multiple parents are not a general requirement or guarantee of inheritance.

Question 77

Which concept in the object-oriented model allows different classes to share the same method name but with different implementations?

  • A. Polymorphism
  • B. Abstraction
  • C. Encapsulation
  • D. Inheritance

Source

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 188

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Distinguish the subtype relationship from use through a common interface.

Study-guide sections

ADB03 · Inheritance, polymorphism and safe substitutability

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

ADB03 · Inheritance, polymorphism and safe substitutability

Correct answer: A — Polymorphism.

ADB03 illustrates Shape.area dispatching to Circle.area or Rectangle.area according to the actual object. The common operation name has different compatible implementations, which is polymorphism. Inheritance can provide the subtype structure used by that mechanism, but is not itself the runtime dispatch behavior. Abstraction and encapsulation concern contracts and implementation access instead.

Evidence in the complete study note

Subtype polymorphism lets a superclass/interface reference denote objects of different compatible subclasses. The same operation can dispatch to different implementations: Shape.area() calls Circle.area() or Rectangle.area() according to the actual object. This is not arbitrary conversion of an object into an unrelated class, nor dynamic class mutation. Inheritance establishes a subtype relationship; polymorphism uses that relationship through a common interface. Distinguish inheritance as a structural relationship from polymorphism as a use of that relationship at runtime.ADB03

Choice by choice

A · correct — Polymorphism lets the same interface operation invoke different implementations for compatible object types.

B · incorrect — Abstraction exposes a relevant contract rather than selecting among differing method implementations.

C · incorrect — Encapsulation controls internal access rather than providing type-dependent method dispatch.

D · incorrect — Inheritance supplies a structural subtype relation; polymorphism describes the differing implementations through a common interface.

Question 79

ADB02 · Encapsulation, abstraction and object associations

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

ADB02 · Encapsulation, abstraction and object associations

Correct answer: C — Links and interactions between objects.

ADB02 defines association as links between objects, commonly implemented with references, and describes methods invoking operations on other objects. Correct answer: A — Rollback recovery

Undo restores before images and removes after images; failed transactions that updated the database must roll back (p.107). This directly answers the specific action, although undo may be one phase of broader crash recovery.

Evidence in the complete study note

Undo restores before-images of incomplete effects, usually traversing that transaction's updates backward. Redo installs logged after-images when necessary, usually forward. Evidence in the complete study note

Transaction failures include invalid operations, constraint violations and concurrency-control aborts. Enforcing concurrency can deliberately abort work; it does not prevent every transaction failure. A system crash loses volatile memory while disks may survive. Media failure damages persistent storage and normally requires restoring a backup, then replaying available archived logs. Human mistakes may require point-in-time restoration before the bad committed operation.ADB26
Restart recovery restores a valid database after a crash while preserving durable commits and removing incomplete effects.ADB26
Recovery may start analysis at the checkpoint but redo from an earlier required log position.ADB30

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Rollback is an undo component rather than the overall process.

B · incorrect — Checkpoint-assisted work guides restart rather than naming its umbrella process.

C · correct — Restart recovery names the complete restoration after this system crash.

D · incorrect — The stated intact persistent storage does not call for restoring a separate backup.

Question 101

In a conventional transaction-log system, which listed mechanisms use logged updates or checkpoint/log state for undo or restart? Select all that apply. Backup recovery in D means restoring only a standalone full backup, without replaying archived logs.

  • A. Rollback recovery
  • B. Checkpoint recovery
  • C. Restart recovery
  • D. Backup recovery

Adapted from

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 213

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Track durable-write ordering and distinguish reversing incomplete work from installing logged effects.

Study-guide sections

ADB27 · WAL, undo and redo

ADB30 · Checkpoints and recovery boundaries

ADB26 · Classify failures and choose the starting resource

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

ADB27 · WAL, undo and redo

ADB30 · Checkpoints and recovery boundaries

ADB26 · Classify failures and choose the starting resource

Correct answers (select all): A, B, C — A. Rollback recovery; B. Checkpoint recovery; C. Restart recovery

Logged rollback uses before-images to remove incomplete effects. Checkpoint-assisted recovery combines durable recovery state with relevant log history, and log-based restart uses that history to preserve commits and remove incomplete work. All three fit the specified model. A standalone backup restore instead copies a separately stored database image; the question excludes archived-log replay from D so that this alternative does not overlap.

Evidence in the complete study note

Write-ahead logging requires the update log needed for recovery to reach stable storage before the corresponding changed data page reaches disk. To acknowledge a durable commit, force the transaction's required log records, including its commit record, to stable storage. A buffer can be changed before that log flush; WAL orders durable writes, not every CPU assignment.ADB27
Undo restores before-images of incomplete effects, usually traversing that transaction's updates backward.ADB27
Active transactions can span the checkpoint, so their relevant earlier updates can still need undo.ADB30

Choice by choice

A · correct — The logged rollback uses before-images for undo.

B · correct — Checkpoint-assisted recovery uses recovery-state records and relevant log history.

C · correct — The specified log-based restart uses durable transaction history.

D · incorrect — A standalone image restore without log replay does not use the specified logged recovery mechanism.

Transaction failures include invalid operations, constraint violations and concurrency-control aborts. Evidence in the complete study note

A distributed database contains logically related data across networked sites, managed as a coordinated system. A homogeneous system uses compatible DBMS technology across sites; a heterogeneous system integrates differing DBMSs, data models, schemas or interfaces. Question 109

Study-guide sections

ADB35 · Transparency: what exactly is hidden?

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

ADB35 · Transparency: what exactly is hidden?

Correct answer: C — Location transparency

Location transparency hides the physical site holding a named logical object. Fragmentation transparency instead hides the existence and reconstruction of fragments, while replication transparency hides which copy is used and how copies are maintained. Those properties can coexist in a distributed database, so a vague single-logical-database experience would not identify only one. The revised stem isolates hidden site placement. Local-only access restricts what can be accessed rather than making remote placement transparent.

Evidence in the complete study note

Location transparency hides which site holds a named object. Fragmentation transparency hides the existence and reconstruction of fragments: users query the whole logical relation. Replication transparency hides which copy is used and how copies are maintained. The broad single-logical-database experience may involve all three.ADB35

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Incorrect: restricting access to local data does not hide the placement of a named distributed object.

B · incorrect — Incorrect: fragmentation transparency hides splitting and reconstruction, not specifically the object's physical site.

C · correct — Correct: location transparency hides which physical site stores the named object.

D · incorrect — Incorrect: replication transparency hides copy selection and maintenance, not specifically site placement.

Homogeneity is defined by using the same or compatible DBMS technology across sites. A · incorrect — Copying all data everywhere is not required for the stated integration.

B · incorrect — The scenario retains differing DBMSs rather than replacing all with one standard.

C · correct — Interoperable communication is needed to exchange requests and results.

D · correct — Mappings must reconcile schema meanings without requiring identical local schemas.

Question 116

What is the role of a distributed transaction coordinator in a distributed database system?

  • A. It ensures the consistency of data across all sites.
  • B. It manages the distribution and retrieval of data across multiple sites.
  • C. It controls the access permissions of users in the system.
  • D. It handles the physical storage of data at each site.

Source

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 233

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Distinguish coordinated transaction outcome from concurrent access and local storage.

Study-guide sections

ADB39 · Distributed atomic commit and Oracle commit points

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

ADB39 · Distributed atomic commit and Oracle commit points

ADB06 · Transactions, ACID and state transitions

ADB38 · Distributed query plans and semijoin arithmetic

ADB24 · Security, integrity and inference control

Correct answer: A — It ensures the consistency of data across all sites.

Global consistency is required of concurrency/recovery (p.122). Under the primary-site technique a coordinator manages transaction concurrency and commit (p.123). A is supported in that transaction-coordination sense, rather than as an unconditional guarantee against every error.

Evidence in the complete study note

Two-phase commit (2PC) first asks participants to prepare and durably promise they can commit. If all vote yes, the coordinator records commit durably and tells participants; otherwise it decides abort. A prepared participant must retain enough state to obey the final decision. Coordinator/communication failure can leave it in doubt and block progress until the decision is learned. Timeout after preparation is not permission to invent a commit or abort.ADB39
The transaction coordinator coordinates decisions rather than physically storing every site's rows.ADB39
Distributed processing decomposes a logical query, localizes referenced relations to fragments/replicas, chooses global placement/order and optimizes local subplans.ADB38

Choice by choice

A · correct — Coordination of concurrency and commit maintains transaction consistency across sites.

B · incorrect — Query transfer/retrieval is a separate distributed-query task.

C · incorrect — User permissions are authorization, not commit coordination.

D · incorrect — Local physical storage is not the primary coordinator’s stated function.

Question 117

Which listed approaches are replication policies or transfer methods in distributed databases, allowing dimensions to coexist? Select all that apply.

  • A. Eager replication
  • B. Lazy replication
  • C. Snapshot replication
  • D. Incremental replication

Adapted from

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 234

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Separate copy placement, propagation timing and update-maintenance cost.

Study-guide sections

ADB37 · Replication policies and their costs

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

ADB37 · Replication policies and their costs

Correct answers (select all): A, B, C, D — A. Eager replication; B. Lazy replication; C. Snapshot replication; D. Incremental replication

Eager and lazy replication differ in when propagation occurs relative to the acknowledgment or commit point. Snapshot and incremental replication differ in whether a copy or changes are transferred. These are legitimate replication dimensions and can coexist, so all four qualify. The question asks for recognized approaches rather than claiming that one policy is most prevalent or universally preferable.

Evidence in the complete study note

Full replication places the whole database at every relevant site; partial replication copies selected fragments to selected sites; nonredundant allocation stores each fragment once. Copies improve read locality and can improve availability but require storage and update propagation. They can also spread mistakes, so replication does not replace independent backups.ADB37
Eager/synchronous replication coordinates propagation before the specified commit/acknowledgment point, increasing update latency.ADB37
Snapshot replication transfers a copy at intervals; incremental replication transfers changes.ADB37

Choice by choice

A · correct — Eager replication coordinates propagation before the specified acknowledgment or commit point.

B · correct — Lazy replication propagates changes later and can expose stale reads or require conflict handling.

C · correct — Snapshot replication distributes a copy at intervals rather than necessarily sending each individual update.

D · correct — Incremental replication transfers changes and can coexist with a propagation-timing policy.

Question 118

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

ADB38 · Distributed query plans and semijoin arithmetic

Correct answers (select all): A, B, C, D — A. Cost of query execution; B. Size of the database; C. Network bandwidth; D. Data replication

Execution cost summarizes the resources consumed by a candidate plan. Relation sizes affect scans and intermediate work, network bandwidth affects data-transfer time, and replica placement changes which copies are available near the computation. All these inputs can alter a distributed strategy's cost. They are complementary considerations rather than competing names for one exclusively important factor.

Evidence in the complete study note

A cost model estimates resources for a candidate plan: page I/O, CPU, memory, temporary storage and network traffic. Catalog statistics include row/page counts, distinct values and distributions. Selection with fraction s predicts s×N rows. For non-NULL equijoin keys, a common estimate is |R|×|S|/max(V(R,k),V(S,k)), assuming uniform values and containment of the smaller distinct-value domain within the larger. Adjust counts for NULLs; if either non-NULL input is empty, the result is zero. Skew, correlations or incomplete domain overlap can invalidate this estimate; known disjoint domains give zero matches.ADB19
Distributed processing decomposes a logical query, localizes referenced relations to fragments/replicas, chooses global placement/order and optimizes local subplans.ADB38
Include bytes moved, message latency, bandwidth and local work.ADB38

C · correct — Bandwidth affects transfer time when data or results move between sites.

D · correct — Replica locations affect which copy can serve a query and its communication cost.

Query optimization chooses an efficient execution strategy and minimizes resource usage including response time (p.27). Page 30 explicitly seeks faster queries and the most efficient sequence of steps.

Parsing checks SQL grammar; semantic analysis resolves names, types and access permissions. Translation constructs a logical representation, typically relational algebra or a logical query tree. Parsing checks SQL grammar; semantic analysis resolves names, types and access permissions. Translation constructs a logical representation, typically relational algebra or a logical query tree. Question 122

What is a join operation in query processing?

  • A. Combining tuples from multiple tables based on a common attribute
  • B. Sorting the query result in ascending order
  • C. Grouping the query result based on a specific attribute
  • D. Filtering the query result based on a condition

Source

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 239

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Separate the query's representation from the operations used to calculate its result.

Study-guide sections

ADB-S01 · Query representations and relational operators

ADB18 · Heuristic and semantic query rewrites

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

ADB-S01 · Query representations and relational operators

ADB18 · Heuristic and semantic query rewrites

Correct answer: A — Combining tuples from multiple tables based on a common attribute

The query joins Staff and Branch by matching branchNo (p.27). The heuristic combines a Cartesian product and selection on the join condition into a join (p.41); the distributed example similarly matches Employee.Dno and Department.Dnumber (p.120). A expresses this equijoin case; joins in general need not always use equality or identical attribute names.

Evidence in the complete study note

A relation is represented by a table of tuples. Selection filters its rows by a predicate; projection retains chosen columns. A Cartesian product constructs every pair of input tuples. A matching join combines tuples satisfying its predicate, and can be represented as a selection over a product. Sorting orders results, while grouping collects rows sharing grouping values; these are different operations.ADB-S01
Heuristics reduce intermediate work: push selective row filters toward base tables; replace product followed by a join predicate with a join; project unneeded columns away while retaining join/filter columns; reorder inner joins when equivalence permits; reuse common expressions when worthwhile.ADB18
Cost-based optimization estimates candidate plans instead of relying on rules alone.ADB18

Choice by choice

A · correct — Combining tuples that satisfy the matching attribute condition describes these joins.

B · incorrect — Sorting changes order rather than combining source tuples.

C · incorrect — Grouping builds groups/aggregates, not cross-relation matching.

D · incorrect — Filtering alone selects rows rather than combining related tuples from tables.

Question 123

Which listed index or clustered-storage approaches can speed a suitable query workload, without a claim that any always wins? Select all that apply.

  • A. B-tree index
  • B. Hash index
  • C. Bitmap index
  • D. Clustered index

Adapted from

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 240

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Match the predicate and workload to the access structure or reasons to choose a plan again.

Study-guide sections

ADB23 · Indexes, statistics and re-optimization

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

ADB23 · Indexes, statistics and re-optimization

Correct answers (select all): A, B, C, D — A. B-tree index; B. Hash index; C. Bitmap index; D. Clustered index

B-tree indexes support ordered and range access, hash indexes target equality, and bitmap indexes can support analytic selections. Clustered storage places related rows close together and can reduce access work for suitable queries. Each approach can therefore help an appropriate workload. Space, maintenance and selectivity still matter, so accepting all four does not claim that every query benefits or that one design is universally best.

Evidence in the complete study note

B/B+ tree indexes support ordered and range predicates; hash indexes target equality; bitmap indexes can help some analytic selections. Clustered storage keeps related rows close. An index may reduce reads but adds space and update work; scanning can be faster when most rows qualify. Commonly useful is not a unique property of one index type.ADB23
Avoid universal rules that joins always beat subqueries, functions can never use indexes or more indexes always improve performance.ADB23
Updating statistics does not itself execute the query.ADB23

Choice by choice

A · correct — B-tree indexes support selective ordered and range access for suitable queries.

B · correct — Hash indexes can accelerate equality lookups on the indexed key.

C · correct — Bitmap indexes can accelerate suitable analytic selection workloads.

D · correct — Clustered storage keeps related rows close and can reduce reads for appropriate access patterns.

Question 125

What is query pipelining in query processing?

  • A. Dividing a query into subqueries and executing them in parallel
  • B. Dividing a query into stages and executing them sequentially

ADB22 · Pipelining, parallelism and caching

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

ADB22 · Pipelining, parallelism and caching

Correct answer: D — Dividing a query into multiple stages and executing them concurrently

Pipelined evaluation evaluates several operations simultaneously and passes results directly from one to the next (p.44). D means overlapping producer/consumer stages, not necessarily executing independent whole queries.

Evidence in the complete study note

Materialization stores an intermediate result before the next operator consumes it. Pipelining passes tuples as they become available, overlapping producer and consumer work and reducing temporary I/O. A sort is normally blocking; a hash join must build its hash table before probing can output, though later probe/output can stream. Pipelining does not require separate CPUs.ADB22
Parallel execution uses multiple workers, for example partitioned scans/joins, independent subplans or operator pipelines.ADB22
Specify the kind of query caching being discussed.ADB22

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Parallel independent subqueries are not the defining inter-operator tuple stream.

B · incorrect — Pure sequential completion of each whole stage loses the stated simultaneous overlap.

C · incorrect — Multiple independent queries are not the defining pipeline within an expression tree.

D · correct — Concurrent overlapping stages passing tuples match the explicit definition.

What is query result caching, specifically caching returned answers rather than execution plans or intermediate rows?

Study-guide references

ADB22 · Pipelining, parallelism and caching

ADB19 · Estimate costs, cardinalities and selectivity

Correct answer: A — A. Storing query results for future reuse

Result caching stores a query's returned rows or answer for future reuse. It needs suitable invalidation when underlying data changes. Plan caching instead stores the execution strategy without its returned rows. Intermediate rows retained during one execution are materialization, while database metadata supports optimization. Naming the cached object makes result caching distinct from these other useful storage mechanisms.

Evidence in the complete study note

Parallel execution uses multiple workers, for example partitioned scans/joins, independent subplans or operator pipelines. Interleaving on one CPU is concurrency; simultaneous cores provide parallelism. Result caching reuses answers and needs invalidation when underlying data changes. Plan caching reuses an execution strategy, not the rows returned. Buffer caching keeps data pages; materialization retains intermediate rows. Specify the kind of query caching being discussed.ADB22
Materialization stores an intermediate result before the next operator consumes it.ADB22

Question 128

If power went off while processing a transaction, what should the DBMS do to reverse any changes made to the database?

  • A. Read_transaction
  • B. Fail transaction
  • C. Commit transaction
  • D. Rollback

Source

  • Computer Science Exit Exam practice collection · Question 66

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Track durable-write ordering and distinguish reversing incomplete work from installing logged effects.

Study-guide sections

ADB27 · WAL, undo and redo

ADB06 · Transactions, ACID and state transitions

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

ADB27 · WAL, undo and redo

ADB06 · Transactions, ACID and state transitions

Correct answer: D — Rollback

To reverse changes of an incomplete failed transaction, recovery undoes its effects (p.103) by restoring before images (p.107). This is rollback. A committed transaction instead requires durability, so the answer assumes the interrupted transaction had not committed, as implied by reverse any changes.

Evidence in the complete study note

Write-ahead logging requires the update log needed for recovery to reach stable storage before the corresponding changed data page reaches disk. To acknowledge a durable commit, force the transaction's required log records, including its commit record, to stable storage. A buffer can be changed before that log flush; WAL orders durable writes, not every CPU assignment.ADB27
Undo restores before-images of incomplete effects, usually traversing that transaction's updates backward.ADB27
Atomicity means all effects or none; consistency means correct work preserves integrity rules; isolation controls concurrent interference; durability preserves committed effects despite failure.ADB06

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Reading a transaction is not an undo operation.

B · incorrect — Marking failure does not itself restore old values.

C · incorrect — Committing would preserve rather than reverse the changes.

D · correct — Rollback/undo is the direct reversal mechanism.

Question 129

What is the main difference between homogeneous and heterogeneous distributed databases?

    Source

    • Advanced Database Systems review questions · Question 1

    Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

    Separate coordinated network placement from engine compatibility and semantic integration.

    Study-guide sections

    ADB33 · Distributed, homogeneous and heterogeneous systems

    Answer & Detailed Explanation

    Study-guide references

    ADB33 · Distributed, homogeneous and heterogeneous systems

    Answer: Homogeneous systems use compatible DBMS technology; heterogeneous systems integrate differing DBMSs, models, schemas or interfaces.

    ADB33 defines the distinction through compatibility of database technology and representation. Operating-system differences can occur but do not define heterogeneity. Homogeneous sites need not have identical schemas or automatic replication. Heterogeneous integration requires explicit mappings for names, types and semantics, rather than assuming that common connectivity alone reconciles their meanings.

    Evidence in the complete study note

    A distributed database contains logically related data across networked sites, managed as a coordinated system. A homogeneous system uses compatible DBMS technology across sites; a heterogeneous system integrates differing DBMSs, data models, schemas or interfaces. Different operating systems are possible but do not define the distinction. Same DBMS does not imply identical local schemas, automatic replication or immediate synchronization.ADB33
    ODBC and JDBC provide connectivity interfaces; they do not automatically solve semantic differences or create one distributed transaction.ADB33
    Heterogeneous design must reconcile naming, types, units, identifiers, query capabilities and transaction semantics.ADB33

    Question 130

    Why is data fragmentation useful in distributed databases?

      Source

      • Advanced Database Systems review questions · Question 2

      Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

      Identify whether rows or columns are split and reverse the split to reconstruct the original relation.

      Study-guide sections

      ADB36 · Fragmentation: correctness and reconstruction

      Answer & Detailed Explanation

      Study-guide references

      ADB36 · Fragmentation: correctness and reconstruction

      Answer: Fragmentation improves locality, manageable placement and parallelism by splitting data across useful site boundaries.

      ADB36 splits rows with predicates and columns with projections while preserving reconstruction through unions or key joins. This can place frequently used data near its consumers and allow independent work on pieces. Correct fragments must preserve completeness and required disjointness. Fragmentation alone creates no spare copy, so losing the only site containing a fragment still makes it unavailable.

      Evidence in the complete study note

      Horizontal fragmentation selects row subsets by predicates; their union reconstructs the relation. Check completeness so every original row is represented and disjointness if no overlap is intended. Define an explicit fragment for NULL/other values when needed. Vertical fragmentation projects column subsets and repeats a key or row identifier so joining on it reconstructs the original rows without spurious matches.ADB36
      Partitioning improves locality and parallelism but alone creates no spare copy.ADB36
      Losing the only site containing a fragment makes that fragment unavailable, even while other sites continue.ADB36

      Question 131

      What is the purpose of two-phase locking (2PL) in concurrency control?

        Source

        • Advanced Database Systems review questions · Question 3

        Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

        Track the first lock release and the transaction-completion boundary.

        Study-guide sections

        ADB12 · Two-phase locking and its variants

        Answer & Detailed Explanation

        Study-guide references

        ADB12 · Two-phase locking and its variants

        Answer: 2PL guarantees conflict serializability by separating lock acquisition from release.

        During the growing phase a transaction acquires or upgrades locks; after it releases any lock, the shrinking phase forbids acquiring new ones. For well-formed transactions this guarantees conflict serializability. Basic 2PL can still deadlock and permit cascading aborts, so strict or conservative variants add different protections. It is distinct from distributed two-phase commit.

        Evidence in the complete study note

        Basic 2PL has a growing phase that acquires/upgrades locks and a shrinking phase that releases/downgrades them. Once any lock is released, no new lock may be acquired. The lock point is the instant the final lock is obtained. 2PL guarantees conflict serializability for well-formed transactions, but can deadlock and basic 2PL alone need not prevent cascading aborts.ADB12
        Two-phase locking orders access to data; two-phase commit coordinates a distributed commit decision.ADB12
        Strict 2PL retains exclusive locks until commit/abort.ADB12

        Question 132

        Why is write-ahead logging important for database recovery?

          Source

          • Advanced Database Systems review questions · Question 4

          Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

          Track durable-write ordering and distinguish reversing incomplete work from installing logged effects.

          Study-guide sections

          ADB27 · WAL, undo and redo

          Answer & Detailed Explanation

          Study-guide references

          ADB27 · WAL, undo and redo

          Answer: WAL makes recovery information durable before its changed data pages, enabling safe undo/redo after crashes.

          ADB27 requires needed update logs to reach stable storage before corresponding changed pages. A durable commit also forces required log records, including commit. Recovery can then use before-images for undo and after-images for redo if buffered data was lost. WAL orders durable writes; modifying an in-memory buffer before the log flush does not itself violate it.

          Evidence in the complete study note

          Write-ahead logging requires the update log needed for recovery to reach stable storage before the corresponding changed data page reaches disk. To acknowledge a durable commit, force the transaction's required log records, including its commit record, to stable storage. A buffer can be changed before that log flush; WAL orders durable writes, not every CPU assignment.ADB27
          Redo installs logged after-images when necessary, usually forward.ADB27
          Undo restores before-images of incomplete effects, usually traversing that transaction's updates backward.ADB27

          Question 133

          How does a data warehouse differ from an operational database?

            Source

            • Advanced Database Systems review questions · Question 5

            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

            Distinguish operational transactions, analytical workloads and physical storage layout.

            Study-guide sections

            ADB41 · Warehouses, OLTP, OLAP and columnar storage

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            ADB41 · Warehouses, OLTP, OLAP and columnar storage

            Answer: A warehouse integrates historical data for analysis; an operational database serves frequent business transactions.

            OLTP handles account updates and other frequent operational transactions, while OLAP scans and summarizes large datasets. A warehouse commonly integrates sources through extraction, transformation and loading for historical analysis. These are workload tendencies rather than absolute restrictions: operational databases may retain history, and warehouses may receive updates. Schema and storage choices should follow the actual workload.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            OLTP handles frequent operational transactions, such as account updates; OLAP scans and summarizes large datasets for analysis. A warehouse integrates data for historical analysis, often through extraction, transformation and loading. These are workload tendencies: OLTP can retain history and warehouses can be updated.ADB41

            Question 134

            What does ACID stand for in the context of database transactions?

            • A. Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability
            • B. Accuracy, Consistency, Integrity, Durability
            • C. Atomicity, Concurrency, Isolation, Data
            • D. Availability, Consistency, Isolation, Durability

            Source

            • Advanced Database Systems review questions · Question 1

            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

            Track the transaction's guarantee or lifecycle boundary described by the scenario.

            Study-guide sections

            ADB06 · Transactions, ACID and state transitions

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            ADB06 · Transactions, ACID and state transitions

            Correct answer: A — Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability.

            ADB06 names all four ACID properties and assigns distinct roles: all-or-none effects, preserved invariants, controlled interference and durable commits. Only A lists those names in the correct order. Accuracy, integrity, concurrency, data and availability are related database concepts but do not replace the letters of this established transaction acronym.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            A transaction is a logical unit of database work, including read-only work. Atomicity means all effects or none; consistency means correct work preserves integrity rules; isolation controls concurrent interference; durability preserves committed effects despite failure. A DBMS cannot automatically make incorrect business logic consistent.ADB06

            Choice by choice

            A · correct — It lists the four ACID properties in the proper acronym order.

            B · incorrect — Accuracy and Integrity replace Atomicity and Isolation, changing the defined acronym.

            C · incorrect — Concurrency and Data incorrectly replace Consistency and Durability.

            D · incorrect — Availability is not the A in the ACID transaction acronym.

            Question 135

            Which ACID property ensures that a transaction is treated as an indivisible unit — either all steps succeed or none are applied?

            • A. Consistency
            • B. Isolation
            • C. Atomicity
            • D. Durability

            • Advanced Database Systems review questions · Question 2

            Study-guide sections

            ADB06 · Transactions, ACID and state transitions

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            ADB06 · Transactions, ACID and state transitions

            Correct answer: C — Atomicity.

            The question specifies indivisibility of the transaction effects: partial success must not remain if the transaction fails. ADB06 assigns that guarantee to atomicity. Consistency concerns valid invariants, isolation controls interference, and durability protects already committed work. Those properties support correctness too, but none directly means all-or-none effects.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            A transaction is a logical unit of database work, including read-only work. Atomicity means all effects or none; consistency means correct work preserves integrity rules; isolation controls concurrent interference; durability preserves committed effects despite failure. A DBMS cannot automatically make incorrect business logic consistent.ADB06

            Choice by choice

            A · incorrect — Consistency concerns preserving integrity rules rather than specifically making effects indivisible.

            B · incorrect — Isolation controls interactions between concurrent transactions rather than partial transaction application.

            C · correct — Atomicity applies every transaction effect together or discards the incomplete work.

            D · incorrect — Durability protects committed effects after failure rather than defining all-or-none completion.

            Question 136

            • B. A = 4,250, B = 8,750

            ADB06 · Transactions, ACID and state transitions

            Correct answer: B — A = 4,250 Birr and B = 8,750 Birr.

            The requested transfer subtracts 750 from 5000 and adds 750 to 8000, giving 4250 and 8750. The invariant total remains 13000. A and C also sum to 13000, but implement a different amount or the reverse direction. Preserving the total alone does not implement the specified successful transfer; D loses the credit.

            A transaction is a logical unit of database work, including read-only work.             Question 137

            Which ACID property guarantees that committed transaction changes persist even after a system crash?

            • A. Atomicity
            • B. Consistency
            • C. Isolation
            • D. Durability

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            ADB06 · Transactions, ACID and state transitions

            Correct answer: D — Durability.

            ADB06 defines durability as preserving committed effects despite failure. A system may leave data pages buffered at commit provided durable recovery information can restore the changes after a crash. Atomicity controls partial outcomes, consistency protects declared invariants and isolation controls concurrent interference; they do not name this persistence guarantee.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            A transaction is a logical unit of database work, including read-only work. Atomicity means all effects or none; consistency means correct work preserves integrity rules; isolation controls concurrent interference; durability preserves committed effects despite failure. A DBMS cannot automatically make incorrect business logic consistent.ADB06

            Choice by choice

            A · incorrect — Atomicity means all-or-none effects, not specifically persistence after a successful commit.

            B · incorrect — Consistency concerns valid integrity rules before and after correct work.

            C · incorrect — Isolation controls concurrent interference rather than persistence across a crash.

            D · correct — Durability ensures committed changes survive failures through the supported recovery mechanisms.

            Question 138

            In the Read_item(X) operation, what is the THIRD and final step?

            • A. Store the updated block back to disk
            • B. Find the disk block address containing X
            • C. Copy the disk block into main memory buffer
            • D. Copy item X from the buffer to the program variable named x

            Source

            • Advanced Database Systems review questions · Question 5

            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

            Trace movement between program variables, buffers and disk, or the meaning of a recorded transaction event.

            Study-guide sections

            ADB07 · Read/write operations, buffers and log records

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            ADB07 · Read/write operations, buffers and log records

            Correct answer: D — Copy X from the buffer into the program variable x.

            ADB07 first locates the page containing X, brings it into a buffer if absent and then copies X into a program variable. Thus D is the final conceptual read step. Locating and loading precede it, and storing an updated block to disk belongs to writing/flushing rather than completing read_item. A buffer hit can avoid physical I/O.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            read_item(X) locates X's page, brings it into a buffer if absent, and copies X into a program variable. write_item(X) copies the new program value into the buffered page, marking it dirty. Writing that page to disk can occur later according to the buffer policy; write_item is not inherently an immediate disk flush. Insert and delete also modify data; sorting is a query-processing operation rather than a primitive item update.ADB07

            Choice by choice

            A · incorrect — A read does not update and write the block back to disk.

            B · incorrect — Locating the containing page is the first conceptual step, not the final one.

            C · incorrect — Loading the page into a buffer precedes copying the item into the program variable.

            D · correct — The final read step copies the requested item from its buffer into x.

            Question 139

            A transaction that has started and is currently executing its operations is in which state?

            • A. Committed
            • B. Partially Committed
            • C. Active
            • D. Failed

            Source

            • Advanced Database Systems review questions · Question 6

            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

            Track the transaction's guarantee or lifecycle boundary described by the scenario.

            Study-guide sections

            ADB06 · Transactions, ACID and state transitions

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            ADB06 · Transactions, ACID and state transitions

            Correct answer: C — Active.

            ADB06 defines Active as the state while transaction operations are executing. Partially committed follows completion of the last operation but precedes assured durable commitment. Committed means commitment succeeded, while Failed means execution encountered a failure. Merely starting and continuing its operations therefore places this transaction in Active.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            Active means operations are executing. Partially committed means the last operation finished but durable commitment is not yet assured. Committed means commitment succeeded. A failure leads to Failed, then Aborted after rollback; a transaction may terminate or be restarted as a new attempt. Concurrency control primarily enforces isolation; recovery supports atomicity and durability. Transaction management is the broader subsystem, so both it and recovery management can be legitimate answers to broad responsibility questions.ADB06

            Choice by choice

            A · incorrect — Committed requires successful commitment, which has not occurred while operations are still executing.

            B · incorrect — Partially committed follows the last operation rather than ordinary ongoing execution.

            C · correct — Active is the state during execution of the transaction operations.

            D · incorrect — Failed requires an execution failure, which the stem does not report.

            Question 140

            Which transaction state means all operations executed successfully but the commit has NOT been finalized yet?

The transaction becomes Committed only after commitment succeeds, or can fail before that boundary. Active describes operations still running, while Aborted means rollback completed, so neither matches successful operations awaiting finalized commit.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            Active means operations are executing. Partially committed means the last operation finished but durable commitment is not yet assured. Committed means commitment succeeded. A failure leads to Failed, then Aborted after rollback; a transaction may terminate or be restarted as a new attempt. Concurrency control primarily enforces isolation; recovery supports atomicity and durability.             Question 141

            What does the log record [abort, T] indicate?

            • A. Transaction T has just started execution
            • B. Transaction T committed successfully
            • C. Transaction T was aborted and ALL its changes must be discarded
            • D. Transaction T read a data item

            Source

            • Advanced Database Systems review questions · Question 8

            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

            Trace movement between program variables, buffers and disk, or the meaning of a recorded transaction event.

            Study-guide sections

            ADB07 · Read/write operations, buffers and log records

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            ADB07 · Read/write operations, buffers and log records

            Correct answer: C — T is aborting/aborted and its transaction effects must be discarded.

            ADB07 includes ABORT among conceptual log records and warns that it can mark the start of rollback rather than prove every undo step is already complete. C is correct because it says the changes must be discarded, not that all undo has finished. START, COMMIT and ordinary read activity have different meanings.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            A conceptual log can contain START, UPDATE(T,X,old,new), COMMIT, ABORT and END records. Before-images support undo; after-images support redo. Real systems may use physical or logical records, and need not log every read. COMMIT records successful completion; an ABORT record can mark the start of rollback rather than prove every undo step is complete.ADB07

            A · incorrect — A START record, rather than ABORT, marks beginning transaction execution.

            B · incorrect — COMMIT records successful completion; ABORT means the opposite outcome.

            C · correct — Abort requires discarding transaction effects, though this record need not prove all undo is already complete.

            D · incorrect — The record denotes abort handling rather than a read_item operation.

            Question 143

            The Isolation property of ACID ensures that concurrent transactions:

            • A. Always read the same data at the same time
            • B. Do not interfere with each other; each executes independently
            • C. Commit in the same order they started

            Study-guide references

            ADB06 · Transactions, ACID and state transitions

            ADB09 · Serial schedules, conflicts and precedence graphs

            Correct answer: B — Concurrent work is isolated from improper interference.

            ADB06 defines isolation as controlling interference between concurrent transactions. B captures logical independence under the specified isolation guarantee; it does not mean transactions literally use separate hardware or never wait. Isolation does not require identical reads, start-order commits or universal successful completion. Strong serializable isolation makes behavior equivalent to some serial order.

            A transaction is a logical unit of database work, including read-only work. Atomicity means all effects or none; consistency means correct work preserves integrity rules; isolation controls concurrent interference; durability preserves committed effects despite failure.             A serial schedule executes each transaction's operations consecutively.ADB09

            C · incorrect — Isolation does not require commit order to match transaction start order.

            D · incorrect — Conflicts and failures can still cause aborts; isolation is not a success guarantee.

            Question 147

            Which processing type uses multiple CPUs to execute different transactions simultaneously, achieving higher throughput?

            • A. Sequential processing
            • B. Interleaved processing
            • C. Parallel processing
            • D. Batch processing

            Source

            • Advanced Database Systems review questions · Question 14

            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

            ADB22 · Pipelining, parallelism and caching

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            ADB22 · Pipelining, parallelism and caching

            Correct answer: C — Parallel processing.

            ADB22 distinguishes concurrency by interleaving on one CPU from actual simultaneous work on multiple cores. The stem explicitly uses multiple CPUs to execute different transactions at the same time, making Parallel the correct classification. Batch describes grouping work, and sequential processing performs work in order; neither guarantees the stated simultaneous execution.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            Materialization stores an intermediate result before the next operator consumes it. Pipelining passes tuples as they become available, overlapping producer and consumer work and reducing temporary I/O. A sort is normally blocking; a hash join must build its hash table before probing can output, though later probe/output can stream. Pipelining does not require separate CPUs.ADB22
            Interleaving on one CPU is concurrency; simultaneous cores provide parallelism.ADB22
            Parallel execution uses multiple workers, for example partitioned scans/joins, independent subplans or operator pipelines.ADB22

            D · incorrect — Batch describes grouped submission or handling, not necessarily simultaneous multi-CPU execution.

In particular a DBMS cannot make an incorrect business operation consistent merely by wrapping it in a transaction.
